points.title: Say the routine as chunks
points.rule: Put the day in order with the clock from day 2: a las siete, a la una, por la mañana, por la tarde. Me plus the verb is the I-form for these routines: me levanto, me ducho, me acuesto. Me gusta takes one thing or a verb. Voy, hago, and trabajo stay the chunks you already use.

examples.spanish: Me levanto. Me ducho. Me acuesto.
examples.english: I get up. I shower. I go to bed.
First I have breakfast. Then I work.

grammar.notYet: Te and se, me gustan, and the full reflexive table. Trabajas is a you-form you may hear; the ending pattern is day 10.

phrases.note: A la una uses es la una from day 2. Como here means I eat.

phrases.english: I have dinner with my family.
I go to bed at eleven.

phrases.spanish: Normalmente llego a casa a las seis.
phrases.english: I usually get home at six.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Me levanto a las siete y desayuno un café.
lines.english: I get up at seven and have a coffee for breakfast.

lines.speaker: Lucía
lines.english: Do you work in an office?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: A veces. Hoy trabajo desde casa.
lines.english: Sometimes. Today I work from home.

lines.speaker: Lucía
lines.english: In the afternoon, what do you do?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.english: I exercise. I like to run.

practice.title: Your day, start to finish
practice.instruction: Describe your routine from waking up to going to bed. Use primero, después, and luego, and put a time on at least three actions.
starters: Voy al trabajo. / Trabajo desde casa.
tips: Say me levanto, me ducho, and me acuesto as whole chunks.
Do not aim for a perfect chart. Aim for a full spoken day.
